subject: PraxisHealth SIG follow-up: control verification & evidence gating
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@praxishealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@praxishealth.com
Date: 2028-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SIG request and timeline

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our security team has a few follow-ups after reviewing the SIG questionnaire you submitted with the RFP. The reviewers are asking for:

- A concise crosswalk that maps Redwood controls to PraxisHealth control IDs (we provided our control list as an attachment to the RFP).
- Evidence that tenant isolation and customer data segregation are enforced in multi-tenant hosted deployments (sample config + recent audit sample).
- Clarification on key management: where keys are generated, who has access, and whether HSM-backed KMS is supported in Dedicated/Private options.
- A short extract of telemetry/log samples (with PII redacted) showing retention and access controls.

Can you please confirm an evidence delivery plan and whether SOC 2 attestation and ISO artifacts can be shared under our NDA? We are aiming to close compliance validation by 2028-11-10.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Procurement, PraxisHealth
olivia.chen@praxishealth.com

Attachments: praxis_rfi_controls.xlsx (referenced)

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@praxishealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@praxishealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SIG request and timeline

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Internal owners looped below. High level plan:

1) Control crosswalk: we will provide a one-sheet mapping (Redwood control -> Praxis control ID) and a separate SIG control map spreadsheet for your team to validate.
2) Tenant isolation evidence: attach arch diagram + a sanitized config export showing tenant routing and network segmentation. We can provide a short recorded demo if you want a deeper walkthrough.
3) KMS/key management: we support customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed providers in Private and Dedicated; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS with strict access controls. We'll provide KMS key lifecycle docs and our SOC 2 description.
4) Telemetry/log samples: we will provide a 48-hour sample with PII redacted and a brief narrative describing retention, S3 encryption at rest, and identity access logs.

Can we target an initial packet by 2028-11-03 and a follow-up Q&A call on 2028-11-05? Kimberly, can you confirm legal/NDAs for sharing SOC/ISO artifacts? Aditya, can your team produce the sanitized log extracts and the control map?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments (to follow): redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, arch-diagram-v2.png, sig_control_map_v1.xlsx

From: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@praxishealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@praxishealth.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SIG request and timeline

Irene — thanks. A couple of clarifications from our security ops team before you compile the packet:

- For tenant isolation, our reviewers want to see proof that KV caches or shared inference caches cannot exfiltrate cross-tenant data. A short statement plus the config snippet showing KV namespace separation would be ideal.
- For KMS, Praxis requires the option to use a dedicated customer KMS in our cloud account (not just bring-your-own-key wrapped by Redwood). Is that supported in Dedicated?
- Please include the expected window for evidence redaction review — we typically need 48 hours to request further redactions.

Also, if possible, include the contact for the engineer who can confirm the cache namespacing during a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Michael Reyes
Security Architect, PraxisHealth

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@praxishealth.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@praxishealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-02T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SIG request and timeline

Michael — great questions. Quick answers inline: 

- KV caching: Redwood's serving runtime uses isolated KV namespaces per deployment and customer. We'll include the config snippet that binds a namespace to a tenant ID and a short architect note explaining eviction and access controls. We will also provide a sanitized log showing namespace identifiers (non-PII) being scoped per-tenant.

- Customer KMS in customer account: yes — for Dedicated we can integrate an externally provisioned KMS in the customer's cloud account (we support AWS KMS grants / GCP KMS IAM bindings). For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, full customer-managed KMS is supported with HSM options. We'll include a short operations playbook for key rotation and emergency compromise procedures.

- Redaction window: 48 hours is fine. We'll deliver the packet with the understanding you may request redactions within that window; we will also share a checklist of items that might require longer lead time (e.g., source code snippets).

Engineer for namespace confirmation: Aditya Rao will join the technical call and can demonstrate the KV binding on a demo cluster.

Irene

---
Irene Choi
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@praxishealth.com>, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, procurement@praxishealth.com
Date: 2028-11-03T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisHealth SIG follow-up: control verification & evidence gating

Hi Michael / Olivia — I pulled the artifacts together this morning. Packet highlights (attached):

- redwood_soc2_summary.pdf: SOC 2 Type II report summary and scoping notes.
- sig_control_map_v1.xlsx: a control crosswalk mapping Redwood controls to Praxis control IDs (sheet 1 = mappings; sheet 2 = evidence pointers).
- arch-diagram-v2.png: deployment diagram showing tenant boundary, network ACLs, and KV namespace labeling.
- log-sample.json (sanitized): 48-hour telemetry sample with access events + retention flags (PII removed).
- kms_playbook.pdf: customer KMS integration and rotation steps for Dedicated/Private.

Notes: KV namespaces are implemented as per-tenant prefixes and enforced by the runtime at kernel/daemon level; we include a short kernel log that demonstrates namespace enforcement on write/read. I've redacted any raw token values.

Call availability: I can do a 30-minute call on 2028-11-05 at 10:00 AM ET to demo the namespace enforcement and walk through the log sample. If that works, please send an invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments (included in packet): redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, sig_control_map_v1.xlsx, arch-diagram-v2.png, log-sample-sanitized.json, kms_playbook.pdf

From: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@praxishealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@praxishealth.com>, procurement@praxishealth.com
Date: 2028-11-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisHealth SIG follow-up: control verification & evidence gating

Irene / Aditya — received the packet, thanks. Quick notes after an initial scan:

- Crosswalk looks good; we'll validate mappings with our control owners and get back with any gaps by 2028-11-06.
- The KV namespace kernel snippet and the sanitized logs are helpful; our ops team will run an internal review and may ask for one additional sample that includes an access-review event.
- KMS playbook: we confirm Dedicated integration is acceptable. One legal ask: prior to sharing the full SOC 2 PDF our InfoSec legal team needs to confirm the NDA covers third-party attestations. Kimberly (cc'd) — can you confirm from Redwood's side whether we need an NDA amendment or if the existing NDA covers sharing the attestation?

Call: 2028-11-05 10:00 AM ET works for Michael, Olivia, and our ops lead. Please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Michael

---
Michael Reyes
Security Architect, PraxisHealth
